reading.body:
A single lobbying firm filed 90 AI reports, and its client list runs from Mozilla and Pinterest to Intel, Best Buy and Anthropic.

The pattern is breadth over depth. Fourteen AI filings each for Mozilla and Pinterest, twelve for Americans for Responsible Innovation, eleven for Advamed Imaging, nine for AHIP, seven each for RILA, Best Buy and Intel, five for the National Electrical Manufacturers Association, four for Anthropic. No client dominates. A firm carrying this range is not running one campaign, it is running a portfolio of separate interests that happen to share the word AI.

That matters because AI policy is being shaped by who shows up, and the showing up here is done by consumer platforms, a chipmaker, a retailer, a medical imaging trade group, an insurance trade group and a frontier lab at once. The filings also show concentration on the lobbying side: David Peluso is named on 64 of them, Mj Kenny on 61, Adam Hechavarria and Lisa Kountoupes on 56 each. A handful of people carry most of the firm's AI workload.

What the data does not say is what any of these clients argued. A filing reports that a client lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the counts measure attention and not intent. The data also names only one bill, HR 7757, and only for 2025 or later, so it cannot show which proposals drew the most filings or how positions shifted. Nothing here speaks to data centers, power or compute directly, except that Intel and the electrical manufacturers association appear among the clients.

summary: KOUNTOUPES DENHAM CARR & REID, LLC filed 90 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 320918.
